searchDocs.title: HttpStore
searchDocs.content: HttpStore Saves and loads replays through a plain HTTP backend. The server contract: GET <base> → JSON array of keys GET <base>/<key> → raw replay bytes (404 when missing) PUT <base>/<key> → stores the raw body DELETE <base>/<key> → removes the replay An optional bearer token is sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Requires HttpService to be enabled and runs on the server or in Studio.

searchDocs.title: Flashback
searchDocs.content: Flashback Flashback records gameplay on the server into a compact binary replay and plays it back on the client or inside Studio. Server: local Flashback = require(ReplicatedStorage.Flashback) local rec = Flashback.Recorder.new({ tickRate = 15 }) rec:start() local blob = rec:stop() Flashback.Store.save("match_1", blob) Client or Studio: local player = Flashback.Player.new(blob) player:play() The Studio plugin installs a server Script that calls Flashback.Studio.serve() so play tests can be recorded from the plugin.

searchDocs.title: save​
searchDocs.content: </> Store.save( key: string, blob: buffer, storeName: string? ) → Meta Saves a replay under a key and records it in the index. Yields.

searchDocs.title: load​
searchDocs.content: </> Store.load( key: string, storeName: string? ) → buffer? Loads a replay by key, or nil if it does not exist. Yields.

searchDocs.title: rootOf​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.rootOf(inst: Instance ) → BasePart?  The part whose CFrame stands for an instance: the part itself, a model's PrimaryPart, or its first part. Shared with the Recorder so recorded transforms and snapshot offsets always refer to the same part.

searchDocs.title: segment​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.segment(inst: Instance ) → string Path segment for an instance: its name, followed by #n when other siblings share that name (n counts same-named siblings in child order). Names alone are ambiguous inside many models (several Wheels, several unions called Union), and runtime scripts cannot read UniqueId.

searchDocs.title: child​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.child( parent: Instance , segment: string ) → Instance?  Resolves one segment under parent: an exact name first (names may contain #), then the Name#n form.

searchDocs.title: pathWithin​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.pathWithin( inst: Instance , root: Instance ) → string? Segments of inst below root, joined with /. Nil when inst is not inside root; empty when they are the same instance.

searchDocs.title: resolve​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.resolve( root: Instance , path: string ) → Instance?  Follows a / path from root.

searchDocs.title: pathOf​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.pathOf(inst: Instance ) → string Unique full path from the DataModel, dotted like GetFullName but with #n on ambiguous segments.

searchDocs.title: instanceAt​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.instanceAt(key: string) → Instance?  Walks a dotted path (see pathOf) from the DataModel. Returns nil when any segment is missing.

searchDocs.title: prefetch​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.prefetch(data: buffer) → () Creates a MeshPart template for every mesh id a snapshot uses. Yields on first use of each id; later builds are synchronous. Ids that fail to load fall back to a SpecialMesh at build time.

searchDocs.title: resolveUnion​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.resolveUnion(key: string) → UnionOperation?  Finds the UnionOperation a key refers to: a manual link first, then the instance at the same path the union had when recorded.

searchDocs.title: keys​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.keys(data: buffer) → Keys Reads the source key and the union keys a snapshot depends on without rebuilding it.

searchDocs.title: capture​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.capture( inst: Instance , exclude: ((Instance ) → boolean)? ) → buffer? Captures inst relative to its root part. Returns nil when there is no geometry to capture. Descendants for which exclude returns true are left out along with everything inside them.

searchDocs.title: build​
searchDocs.content: </> Snapshot.build(data: buffer) → Instance  Rebuilds a snapshot as an anchored, non-colliding Part or Model whose pivot matches the original root. A linked prefab is cloned instead, with its pivot moved to the part at the recorded root's path (or name) so recorded transforms land where the original did.

searchDocs.title: createRecorder​
searchDocs.content: </> Studio.createRecorder(opts: StartOptions) → Recorder.Recorder Builds a recorder from plugin settings. Shared with the plugin's local backend so edit-mode and play-mode recordings match. watch is a list such as BasePart.Color,Humanoid.Health (see Recorder.parseWatch).

searchDocs.title: saveBlob​
searchDocs.content: </> Studio.saveBlob( data: buffer, key: string, target: Target, force: boolean ) → SaveResult Saves a finished recording, refusing to overwrite unless forced.

searchDocs.title: serve​
searchDocs.content: </> Studio.serve() → () Creates the RemoteFunction and starts serving. No-op outside Studio.

searchDocs.title: Install​
searchDocs.content: Get the Flashback plugin and press Install module in its widget. That puts the Flashback ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage and a Studio-only helper Script in ServerScriptService.  The module is open source (MIT) with no dependencies, and installs on its own with Wally as kashtheking/flashback; the plugin is paid. See Licensing. The Tests folder inside the module can be deleted from production builds.

searchDocs.title: Moon Animator export
searchDocs.content: Moon Animator export Flashback can write a loaded replay as a Moon Animator 2 save, so you can polish recorded gameplay into a cutscene or trailer shot. Open Moon Animator so the plugin can see it.In the Flashback widget, load a replay from Replays in edit mode (not during a play test).Press Export to Moon Animator. The save is named after the replay. The export includes transforms, recorded properties as property tracks, lifetime transparency for things that spawn and despawn mid-replay, and links to your prefabs where they exist.

searchDocs.title: Playback
searchDocs.content: Playback Play replays on a client or in Studio. local blob = Flashback.Store.load("match_123") local player = Flashback.Player.new(blob, { prototypes = ReplicatedStorage.Prototypes }) player:onEvent("Kill", function(payload, tick) end) player:onChannel("Scores", function(reader, tick) end) player:play() player:setSpeed(0.5) player:seekSeconds(42) player:pause() player:destroy() Proxies live under workspace.FlashbackProxies (or opts.container) with physics disabled and scripts stripped, so playback never touches the live game. See Descriptors for how each proxy is built. Pass autoStep = false to drive the clock yourself with player:step(dt).

searchDocs.title: Licensing
searchDocs.content: Licensing The Flashback module is open source under the MIT licence. Use it, modify it and ship it in any experience, free or paid. The source lives in the library repo and the licence text ships inside the module. The Studio plugin is paid and proprietary. Buying it lets you use it in your own projects. Don't redistribute or resell the plugin. Questions go to the Discord.

searchDocs.title: Layout​
searchDocs.content: Header StringTable KeyframeIndex OpStream

searchDocs.title: Header​
searchDocs.content: field	type	notesmagic	u32	"RPLY" version	u8	3 tickRate	u8	snapshots per second (e.g. 15) placeVersion	u32	game.PlaceVersion — refuse mismatches startUnix	f64	os.time() at record start tickCount	u32	total ticks stringCount	u16 keyframeCount	u16 opBytes	u32	length of OpStream

searchDocs.title: StringTable​
searchDocs.content: stringCount × (u16 len, bytes). Asset descriptors, property names, event names, animation ids, custom channel names all go through this so the op stream only carries u16 ids.

searchDocs.title: KeyframeIndex​
searchDocs.content: keyframeCount × (u32 tick, u32 byteOffset). A keyframe is a tick where every live entity emitted a full XFORM (no delta). Seeking = jump to nearest keyframe ≤ target, replay forward.

searchDocs.title: OpStream​
searchDocs.content: Sequence of ops. Each op starts with u8 opcode.  op	name	payload0	TICK	u32 tick 1	SPAWN	u16 entityId, u16 descriptorStr, u16 parentEntityId (0=none) 2	DESPAWN	u16 entityId 3	XFORM	u16 entityId, u8 mask, [pos: 3×f32] [rot: 3×i16 quantized] 4	PROP	u16 entityId, u16 nameStr, u8 typeTag, value 5	ANIM_PLAY	u16 entityId, u16 animIdStr, u8 handle, u8 fade/100, i16 speed×256 6	ANIM_STOP	u16 entityId, u8 handle, u8 fade/100 7	ANIM_SPEED	u16 entityId, u8 handle, i16 speed×256 8	EVENT	u16 nameStr, u16 payloadStr (JSON) 9	CUSTOM	u16 channelStr, u16 byteLen, bytes 10	TICK_NEXT	(none) advances tick by one 11	XFORM_D	id entityId, u8 mask, deltas (see below) 14	SNAPSHOT	u16 entityId, u32 byteLen, bytes (geometry snapshot, see below)  XFORM mask bits: 1 = position present, 2 = full rotation present, 4 = yaw-only rotation (i16, ±π). Rotation is quantized as axis-angle scaled to i16 (±π → ±32767). Upright entities (up vector within 0.005% of world up) use yaw-only samples and i8 yaw deltas afterwards.id is one byte below 255, otherwise 0xFF then u16. XFORM_D mask bits: 1 = 3×i8 position delta (1/32 stud), 2 = 3×i16 position delta (same unit, for fast movers), 4 = i8 yaw delta (1/64 rad, yaw-only entities), 8 = 3×i8 axis-angle rotation delta (1/128 rad, tilted entities). Deltas accumulate from the last XFORM; the recorder tracks the quantized value so error does not drift. Deltas that overflow, or a switch between yaw-only and tilted, force a new XFORM. Ticks with no changes emit nothing; TICK_NEXT precedes the first op of a new tick. Position is raw f32 (fine for most maps; quantize to i16 with a per-map origin/scale if size matters).

searchDocs.title: SNAPSHOT​
searchDocs.content: Written once per tracked part or model, player characters included. The capture is taken at SPAWN but held back while descendants keep arriving (a character still loading limbs and accessories) and retaken once the entity has been quiet for a second, then written; pending captures are flushed on despawn, stop and finalize. The player keeps the last one it decodes.u8 version (10), u8 isModel, str16 name, str16 sourceKey (unique path when recorded), str16 rootPath (path of the root part inside the entity), u16 unionCount + str16 union keys (the union's unique path when recorded), u16 meshCount + str16 mesh ids (so the player can prefetch MeshParts), then for models a rig block (u8 hasHumanoid, and if setu8 rigType, str16 shirt, str16 pants, str16 shirtGraphic, u8 hasBodyColors + 6×3 u8 colours, then u8 meshCount × CharacterMesh (u8 bodyPart, f64 meshId, f64 baseTextureId, f64 overlayTextureId asset ids)), thenu16 count and per BasePart: u8 kind (0 Part, 1 MeshPart, 2 Wedge, 3 CornerWedge, 4 other, 5 Union), for unions u16 unionKeyIndex, then str16 name, str16 parentPath (slash-joined segments of the wrappers between the entity and the part, rebuilt as Folders), 3×f32 offset from root, 3×i16 rotation, 3×f32 size, 3×u8 color, u16 material, u8 transparency, u8 reflectance, u8 shape, 6×u8 surface types, for meshes str16 meshId, str16 textureId, 3×f32 meshSize, then an optional SpecialMesh block, an optional SurfaceAppearance block, a list of Decals/Textures and an effects list. After the parts comes a joint list: u16 count, per joint u8 kind, str16 name, u16 holderIndex then for kind 1 Weld / 2 Motor6D u16 part0Index, u16 part1Index, C0, C1, and for kind 3 AnimationConstraint / 4 RigidConstraint u16 part0Index, str16 attachment0Name, u16 part1Index, str16 attachment1Name(indices into the part list, 1-based; attachments are rebuilt from the effects list first). The player rebuilds this as an anchored proxy when no prototype is supplied; MeshPart meshes are rebuilt as real MeshParts through AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync (Snapshot.prefetch, which Player.new calls and which yields the first time each mesh id is seen), with a scaled SpecialMesh as fallback; the root part always comes first so it becomes the proxy's PrimaryPart; joints are recreated so animations drive the rig, and rigs get a Humanoid so clothing renders. Union geometry cannot be serialized: on playback a key resolves to the UnionOperation at the recorded path, or to one linked manually through Snapshot.link (the plugin's Prefab links list), and is cloned; otherwise a plain Part of the same size stands in. Linking a snapshot's source key to a prefab (typically kept under ReplicatedStorage) makes the player clone that prefab instead of rebuilding the snapshot at all, which is the way to play back models that cannot be serialized faithfully; the clone's PrimaryPart is moved to the part named like the recorded root so recorded transforms land where the original did.  Effects list: u8 count, per effect u8 class (1 Attachment, 2 Sound, 3 ParticleEmitter, 4 Beam, 5 Trail, 6 Fire, 7 Smoke, 8 Sparkles, 9 PointLight, 10 SpotLight, 11 SurfaceLight), u8 parentIndex (0 = the part, else an earlier attachment), str16 name, u8 propCount and per property u8 propIndex (into the class's property list), u8 tag, value with tags 0 bool, 1 f32, 2 str16, 3 Color3, 4 Vector3, 5 Vector2, 6 NumberRange, 7 NumberSequence (u8 n × time/value/envelope f32), 8 ColorSequence (u8 n × f32 time + Color3), 9 enum name, 10 attachment reference by name. Watched properties (the recorder's Class.Property watch list, whose default covers part appearance, humanoid health and effect state such as Enabled, Playing, Rate, Size, Volume, Brightness) of the entity and the instances inside it are written as PROP ops whose name is a slash path inside the entity as the rebuilt proxy sees it, e.g. Body/Exhaust/Enabled or Hat/Handle/Transparency. Initial values of properties the snapshot already carries (part Color, Transparency, Size, Material, Reflectance and effect state) are not written; only changes are. Attributes of a tracked instance are written as @Name (and set back with SetAttribute), and a tracked model's scale as Scale, the ratio of Model:GetScale() to its value at spawn (applied with ScaleTo). A watched Sound's Playedevent writes <path>/TimePosition = 0 and <path>/Playing = true so restarts of an already playing sound replay. Which properties, attributes, scale, animations and descendants (properties and effects inside the entity) are recorded is set per recorder and overridable per instance through the FlashbackWatch, FlashbackAttributes, FlashbackScale, FlashbackAnimationsand FlashbackDescendants attributes.

searchDocs.title: PROP typeTags​
searchDocs.content: 0 bool, 1 number(f64), 2 string(strId), 3 Color3 (3×u8), 4 Vector3 (3×f32), 5 enum(u16 strId of name).

searchDocs.title: Descriptor strings​
searchDocs.content: A descriptor tells the player how to build a proxy. Convention:  model:<path.in.ReplicatedStorage.Prototypes> — clone a prototypepart:<Shape> — create a bare Part, PROP ops fill Size/Color/Materialchar:<userId> — player character; rebuilt from its SNAPSHOT (limbs, accessories, clothing, body colours, joints), falling back to Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromUserId for recordings without onesub:<path> — a BasePart inside a tracked ancestor; the player drives the part at that path inside the parent proxy instead of creating a new one. Tagged parts jointed to a tracked ancestor (Motor6D, Weld, WeldConstraint) are not written at all: the rig's own joints and recorded animation tracks move them. When every joint holding such a part disappears it is spawned as a sub: entity from that tick; the player removes the proxy's joint and drives itmodel:<name> is also used for Tools carried inside a tracked entity: they spawn as child entities (parent id set) with their own snapshot when equipped and despawn when they leaveasset:<assetId> — InsertService (rarely worth it; prefer prototypes)

searchDocs.title: Paths​
searchDocs.content: Every path (sub: descriptors, PROP names, snapshot parent paths, source and union keys) is made of segments that are the instance name, suffixed with #n when siblings share that name (n counts same-named siblings in child order), e.g.Wheel#2/Transparency. A segment is resolved by exact name first, then by the Name#n form, so names containing # still work.

searchDocs.title: Size budget (rough)​
searchDocs.content: 20 players @ 15 Hz, position+rotation each tick: 20 × 15 × (1+2+1+12+6) ≈ 6.6 KB/s ≈ 4 MB per 10 min raw. Delta thresholds (skip XFORM if moved < 0.05 studs / 0.5°) usually cut that 3–5×. Chunk at ~3.5 MB per DataStore key or push to your own backend.

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: option	default	meaningtickRate	15	snapshots per second keyframeEvery	300	ticks between full transforms trackCharacters	true	tag player characters automatically

searchDocs.title: Extending​
searchDocs.content: watchProperties(className, props) records bool, number, string, Color3, Vector3 and Enum properties on matching entities.event(name, payload) queues a JSON event for the next tick.registerChannel(name, writer) calls writer(w, tick) every tick with a binary writer for anything the generic system does not cover.custom(channel, buffer) queues a one-off binary payload.Animations on tracked models are captured from Animator.AnimationPlayed.

searchDocs.title: Descriptors​
searchDocs.content: The descriptor attribute tells playback what proxy to build:  descriptor	proxychar:<userId>	Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromUserId model:<name>	clone of <name> under opts.prototypes, else rebuilt from the recorded geometry snapshot part:<Shape>	rebuilt from the snapshot (or a bare Part), shape overridden when given anything else	magenta placeholder part so missing prototypes show up

searchDocs.title: DataStore​
searchDocs.content: Flashback.Store saves to DataStoreService in 3 MB chunks with a small metadata record and an index of keys.  Flashback.Store.save(key, blob, storeName?) Flashback.Store.load(key, storeName?) -- buffer? Flashback.Store.meta(key, storeName?) Flashback.Store.list(storeName?) -- { string } Flashback.Store.remove(key, storeName?)   Pass a store name as the last argument to isolate environments. Saving in Studio needs Studio API access enabled.

searchDocs.title: HTTP​
searchDocs.content: Flashback.HttpStore talks to any HTTP backend with the same operations. Requires HttpService enabled.  request	responseGET <base>	JSON array of keys GET <base>/<key>	raw replay bytes, 404 when missing PUT <base>/<key>	stores the raw body DELETE <base>/<key>	removes it  An optional bearer token is sent as Authorization.

searchDocs.title: export​
searchDocs.content: </> MoonExport.export( player: Player.Player, name: string ) → StringValue  Steps player from its first tick to its last and writes the save. Only meaningful in edit mode, where the player advances animators itself. Returns the save StringValue.

searchDocs.title: Header​
searchDocs.content: Shows whether the Flashback module is installed. Click the text to select it in the Explorer, or the X to uninstall it.

searchDocs.title: Install module​
searchDocs.content: Copies Flashback into ReplicatedStorage, tags it FlashbackModule, and adds a FlashbackStudio Script to ServerScriptService. You can move the module anywhere under ReplicatedStorage, ServerStorage or ServerScriptService; the plugin and the server script find it by tag.  The script serves a Studio-only RemoteFunction so the plugin can record play tests from the client view. It does nothing outside Studio.

searchDocs.title: Record​
searchDocs.content: The big button starts and stops a session. Elapsed time and estimated size update live, and the replay saves on stop. Existing session names are never overwritten without an explicit Overwrite click.  Recording in a play test happens on the server and captures gameplay. Recording in edit mode captures whatever you move by hand.

searchDocs.title: Tracked instances​
searchDocs.content: Tag selection and Untag selection add or remove the current Explorer selection. Player characters and their limbs are always recorded. Select all tagged selects everything that is tagged.  Press Properties on a tagged instance to choose what is recorded for it: apply a preset (such as Character), or toggle Record animations, Record attributes, Record model scale and Record descendants. These choices are stored as attributes on the instance itself, and the X untags it.

searchDocs.title: Settings​
searchDocs.content: Session name, storage, tick rate, keyframe interval and which properties to capture. Settings persist across Studio runs and can be saved as named presets.  Storage is one of:  DataStore, with an optional name suffix to keep environments apart. Needs Studio API access.HTTP server, see Storage.This computer: the replay is base64-encoded into the plugin's settings file. Keep it to short sessions.

searchDocs.title: Replays​
searchDocs.content: Refresh list shows the stored sessions, each with Load and Delete. Loading one plays it back right in the viewport, with:  a scrubber with the current time, Play/Pause, and speed presets from 0.25x to 4x (or drag the speed slider);Loop and Reverse;Prefab links: select a model (for example in ReplicatedStorage) and press Link selected to have playback clone it instead of rebuilding it from the recording;Export to Moon Animator, shown when Moon Animator is loaded; see Moon Animator;Unload replay to remove the playback proxies.

searchDocs.title: readHeader​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.readHeader(blob: buffer) → Header Reads only the header of a replay buffer without decoding the op stream.

searchDocs.title: _characterTemplate​
searchDocs.content: </> Player._characterTemplate( self: Player, userId: number ) → Instance?  Fetches a character model once per user and reuses clones afterwards, so rewinding never waits on the network or spawns duplicates.

searchDocs.title: cframeAt​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.cframeAt( _self: Player, e: Entity, t: number ) → CFrame?  Returns the interpolated CFrame of an entity at a fractional tick, or nil before its first sample.

searchDocs.title: _trackSpeed​
searchDocs.content: </> Player._trackSpeed( self: Player, recorded: number ) → number Speed an animation track should run at: its recorded speed scaled by the playhead speed, and zero while paused.

searchDocs.title: step​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.step( self: Player, dt: number ) → () Advances playback by dt seconds and renders. Called automatically each frame unless autoStep is false. In Studio edit mode animation tracks do not advance on their own, so animators are stepped here. In reverse the playhead runs backwards; transforms interpolate either way, and proxies are rebuilt from spawn only when the playhead crosses a tick that carries discrete state.

searchDocs.title: setReverse​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.setReverse( self: Player, reverse: boolean ) → () When on, playing runs the playhead backwards from its current position.

searchDocs.title: setLoop​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.setLoop( self: Player, loop: boolean ) → () When on, reaching the end restarts from the first tick instead of pausing.

searchDocs.title: seek​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.seek( self: Player, tick: number ) → () Jumps to a tick. Seeking backwards rebuilds proxies so discrete state is replayed from spawn. Seeking forwards applies entity state without firing event or channel handlers. Ticks start at 1, so seeking to 0 shows the first recorded state rather than empty proxies.

searchDocs.title: _rewind​
searchDocs.content: </> Player._rewind( self: Player, tick: number ) → () Rebuilds every proxy so discrete state is replayed from spawn up totick.

searchDocs.title: links​
searchDocs.content: </> Player.links(self: Player) → {Link} Everything in this replay that can be linked to an instance in Studio: recorded models (link a prefab to clone it instead of the snapshot) and the unions inside them. Link with Snapshot.link and reload.

searchDocs.title: parseWatch​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.parseWatch(list: string) → {[string]: {string}} Parses a watch list such as BasePart.Color,Humanoid.Health into the class -> properties table watchProperties uses.

searchDocs.title: watchProperties​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.watchProperties( self: Recorder, className: string, props: {string} ) → () Records the named properties of every tracked instance that IsA className. Initial values are written on spawn and changes are written each tick. Limbs and other jointed sub-parts are skipped; their look comes from the playback rig.

searchDocs.title: registerChannel​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.registerChannel( self: Recorder, name: string, writer: ChannelWriter ) → () Registers a per-tick binary writer. The player must register a reader for the same channel name.

searchDocs.title: event​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.event( self: Recorder, name: string, payload: {[string]: any}? ) → () Queues a discrete gameplay event. The payload is JSON encoded and delivered to player-side handlers registered with the same name.

searchDocs.title: custom​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.custom( self: Recorder, channel: string, data: buffer ) → () Queues an ad-hoc binary payload on a channel.

searchDocs.title: track​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.track( self: Recorder, inst: Instance ) → () Explicitly tracks an instance without tagging it.

searchDocs.title: _recheckJoints​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._recheckJoints( self: Recorder, e: Entity ) → () Gives a limb its own entity once nothing holds it to the rig any more (joints broken on death, a weld destroyed), so its fall is recorded.

searchDocs.title: _spawn​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._spawn( self: Recorder, e: Entity ) → () Writes SPAWN and starts following an entity: props, snapshot, animations, tools carried inside it and sounds played on it.

searchDocs.title: _capture​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._capture( self: Recorder, e: Entity ) → buffer? Snapshot of an entity without the geometry of entities carried inside it (an equipped tool), which have snapshots of their own.

searchDocs.title: _pollTracks​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._pollTracks( self: Recorder, e: Entity ) → () Tracks are polled each tick instead of trusting Stopped, which does not fire reliably for tracks replicated from a client, so a stop lands within one tick of the track going idle.

searchDocs.title: _flushSnapshot​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._flushSnapshot( self: Recorder, e: Entity ) → () Writes the entity's geometry once. The capture taken at spawn is held back while descendants keep arriving (a character still loading limbs and accessories) and replaced by a fresh capture once the entity has been quiet for a second, so a replay carries one snapshot per entity instead of one per arrival. Pending captures are flushed on untrack, stop and finalize; the player keeps the last snapshot it decodes.

searchDocs.title: _descendantProps​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._descendantProps( _self: Recorder, e: Entity, d: Instance ) → {string}? Properties the entity's watch list names for an instance: the union of every listed class it IsA (so BasePart.Color and Part.Shape both apply to a Part). Nil when nothing matches.

searchDocs.title: _writeProp​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._writeProp( self: Recorder, e: Entity, inst: Instance , name: string, key: string, v: any, force: boolean ) → () Writes one PROP op when the value changed since the last tick. On the spawn tick (force) values the snapshot already carries are only remembered, not written.

searchDocs.title: _writeProps​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._writeProps( self: Recorder, e: Entity, force: boolean ) → () Watched properties of the entity and its descendants, its attributes (written as @Name) and, for models, the scale relative to spawn (written as Scale).

searchDocs.title: _writeTick​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder._writeTick(self: Recorder) → () Emits the tick marker lazily so idle ticks cost nothing.

searchDocs.title: snapshot​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.snapshot(self: Recorder) → () Writes one tick. Called automatically while running, and callable directly for deterministic stepping.

searchDocs.title: step​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.step( self: Recorder, dt: number ) → () Advances the recorder clock by dt seconds, emitting as many ticks as elapsed.

searchDocs.title: stop​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.stop(self: Recorder) → buffer Stops recording and returns the finished replay buffer.

searchDocs.title: finalize​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.finalize(self: Recorder) → buffer Assembles header, string table, keyframe index and op stream into a buffer. Safe to call while running to get a partial replay.

searchDocs.title: byteCount​
searchDocs.content: </> Recorder.byteCount(self: Recorder) → number Approximate size in bytes of the replay if finalized now.

searchDocs.title: newWriter​
searchDocs.content: </> Serializer.newWriter(initial: number?) → Writer Creates a writer with an initial capacity. The buffer doubles as needed.

searchDocs.title: writeRotation​
searchDocs.content: </> Serializer.writeRotation( w: Writer, cf: CFrame ) → () Writes the rotation of a CFrame as an axis-angle vector quantized to 3 x i16.

searchDocs.title: rotationFromDelta​
searchDocs.content: </> Serializer.rotationFromDelta( x: number, y: number, z: number ) → CFrame  Rotation delta from three i8 axis-angle components in 1/ROT_Q radians.

searchDocs.title: isYawOnly​
